intuition: Enumerating every substring repeats frequency work across heavily overlapping ranges. Instead of asking how many unique letters each substring contains, reverse the counting perspective: for one particular character occurrence, how many substrings count that occurrence as unique?

Let previous and next be the neighboring indices containing the same character, using -1 and n when a neighbor is absent. A substring containing the occurrence at p may start after previous through p, and may end from p through next-1. These choices are independent, giving (p-previous)*(next-p) valid substrings for that one occurrence.

A left-to-right scan does not know next immediately. Store the last two indices of each character; when its next occurrence arrives, the middle occurrence’s contribution becomes computable. After the scan, finalize the last occurrence of each character using n as its missing next boundary. Summing occurrence contributions counts every unique-character event exactly once, even for equal substring text at different positions. Unique means frequency exactly one, so a substring containing two copies contributes nothing for that character.

steps: For ABA, start with result=0 and no remembered character positions. At index 0, A receives the pair (-1,0); its placeholder contribution is zero.
At index 1, B receives (-1,1), again with zero placeholder contribution.
At index 2, A has before=-1 and previous=0. Its earlier occurrence now contributes (0-(-1))*(2-0)=2; store A positions (0,2).
Finalize A with string boundary 3: (2-0)*(3-2)=2, bringing result to 4.
Finalize B: (1-(-1))*(3-1)=4. Return 8; the two A occurrences each count only substrings excluding their equal neighbor.

codeNotes.note: Two remembered positions provide the left boundary of the previous occurrence when its right boundary arrives.
The two factors count independent start and end choices that include the previous occurrence but exclude equal neighboring characters.
The final occurrence of each letter has no later equal character, so the string boundary supplies its last possible right limit.
